Task scheduling

Learn how to create scheduled tasks that can be run crontab-like, repeatedly or just once.

Experimental: This is an experimental resource that is being considered for addition and may be subject to change or refactoring.

Setup

Before starting, you need to configure the scheduling software available on the operating system to execute the tasks. If the environment uses crontab, you can run the command that performs the automated configuration:

./run schedule:enable

Once configured, it can be automatically removed from the crontab by running:

./run schedule:disable

Manually configuring:

If the automated command is not supported by the environment, it is still possible to manually add a similar instruction to the crontab (adjust the paths):

* * * * * /usr/bin/php /path/to/my-app/run schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1

Creating tasks

It is possible to schedule functions, existing commands, and shell commands. To schedule a function, use:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Scheduling\Task; $mytask = $scheduler->call('mytask1', function (Task $task) { echo 'Hello World!'; }); // Defines a task to be executed every hour. $mytask->interval(3600);

To schedule an existing command, follow the example:

// Creates the command `php run sample`, which can be executed in the terminal. $mycommand = $console->action('sample', function (Command $command, array $options, array $residues) { echo 'Hello World!'; }); // Schedules the command to be executed according to the next instruction. $mytask = $scheduler->command('mytask2', $mycommand); // Configures the schedule to run at the 10-minute mark. $mytask->interval(600);

It is also possible to schedule arbitrary commands—for example, running VACUUM on Postgres databases at regular intervals:

// Sets the task to run on the 1st of every month at 03:00 AM (UTC). $scheduler->shell('mytask3', 'vacuumdb -d my_database')->cron(0, 3, 1, '*', '*');

Another example using the systemd-tmpfiles program.

// Performs cleanup every day at 23:30 (UTC). $scheduler->shell('mytask4', 'systemd-tmpfiles --clean')->at(23, 30);

Testing a task

To test a task, regardless of the schedule, simply run the command:

./run schedule:run --task mytask1

Configuring the schedule

When adding a task, it is necessary to configure the trigger time and whether execution should occur in the background using the following methods:

Comando Descrição
cron($minute, $hour, $day, $month, $weekday) Schedule the task using crontab-style fields.
interval(int $seconds) Schedule the task to run repeatedly at the specified interval in seconds, counting from its last execution.
once(string|DateTime $datetime) Schedule the task to run exactly once at (or after) the specified date/time. Once executed, it will not run again.
at(int $hour, int $minute) Shortcut to schedule the task for daily execution at a fixed time. Equivalent to cron($minute, $hour, '*', '*', '*').
runInBackground(bool $enable) Marks this task to be dispatched as an independent background process, rather than running synchronously within the scheduler process.

Since most methods return the instance of the Inphinit\Experimental\Scheduling\Task class itself, it is possible to use them like this:

$scheduler ->command('mytask', $mycommand) ->cron(30, 16, 1, '*', '*') ->runInBackground(true);

Running in the background

Multiple tasks scheduled for the same time will be executed sequentially, based on the order in which they were defined. Long-running tasks can cause subsequent tasks to start much later than expected. To execute a long task without having to wait for it to start, you should use the runInBackground() method, which allows for background execution. Example:

$scheduler->call(function () { ... })->at(14, 30)->runInBackground(true); $scheduler->call(function () { ... })->at(14, 30)->runInBackground(true);

Changing timeZone

By default, all tasks are executed based on UTC, but it is possible to explicitly configure the once() method to execute a task at a specific time:

use Inphinit\Experimental\Scheduling\Task; $time_zone = new DateTime('2030-01-01', new DateTimeZone('America/Sao_Paulo')); // It will execute on 2030-01-01 at 12:00:00 $scheduler->call('mytask3', function (Task $task) { echo 'Hello World!'; })->once($time_zone);

To set the time zone for all tasks, the method to use is $scheduler->setTimeZone() in system/console.php, as shown in the example:

$time_zone = new DateTimeZone('America/Sao_Paulo'); $scheduler->setTimeZone($time_zone); // Runs every day at 10:00 AM São Paulo time. $scheduler->call(function () { ... })->at(10, 0); // Runs every day at 3:30 PM São Paulo time. $scheduler->call(function () { ... })->at(15, 30); // Runs every day at 8:00 PM São Paulo time. $scheduler->call(function () { ... })->at(20, 0);
